text: On a wet Tuesday in Brevik, the station’s pale dish slowly tracked the evening sky as Orbiton Systems formally took over the ground station lease, ending months of speculation in the coastal district. The agreement, signed in late October with the municipal port authority, covers the rebuilt control house, two feeder arrays and the fiber link installed after the winter storms. According to the company, Orbiton will use the site to relay telemetry for its low-orbit communications fleet, with first commercial handoffs expected by March. Brevik’s station, once a modest maritime receiver in the 1980s, has become the latest prize in the region’s quiet satellite race, drawing interest from engineers, traders and residents alike.
